# dsh-mcp-manager
简体中文 | English
> Local **0.13.3 unreleased candidate**: see the release notes for cumulative changes, provenance an
d verification limits. It supersedes 0.13.2.
**MCP server manager for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** — a Settings → MCP page where you add MCP servers
once (remote HTTP or local stdio process), authenticate HTTP servers with **OAuth in the browser**,
and expose their tools either directly or through a compact on-demand broker.
The built-in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` only accepts a static `headers` config — it has no OAuth
support and no local stdio transport. This plugin fills that gap:
- **OAuth (authorization code + PKCE)** with spec-compliant discovery, RFC 7591 dynamic client regis
tration, `refresh_token` rotation, and auto-reconnect across restarts — one browser login, then it k

eeps working.
- **Registration identity and secret** (RFC 7591): the `client_name` sent to the regis
tration endpoint is `dsh-mcp-manager-<server>` by default and configurable per server (**Client name
**) for providers that gate registration on an exact name. When the authorization server advertises
`client_secret_post`, the client registers confidentially: the issued `client_secret` is stored in t
he 0600 state file and sent on token exchange and refresh (never in a view, response or log). For a
dynamically registered client, a changed client name — or a new GUI origin — re-registers and drops

the old client's tokens; a manually configured Client ID is unaffected.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements
- DeepSeek Harness, web profile for the Settings → MCP page (`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`). On a profi
le without a GUI webserver (headless/tui) the plugin still registers MCP tools and connects servers

— only the settings page is missing.
- Node.js `^22.19` or `>=24`; pnpm on your `PATH`
- Verified DS
H releases are declared one by one in `package.json` → `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` (`0.1.2-rc.1`
ompatible`; supported range `>=0.1.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`). Releases that are not listed are untested, not d
eclared broken. These declarations are backed by disposable-profile runs: install into a scratch `$D
SH_HOME`, boot the `web` profile (`GET /mcp-manager/api/ping` → 200), boot the `headless` profile an
d confirm the agent setup applies (on `0.1.5-*` a registered `mcp__<server>__<tool>` is also visible
to the agent), then delete the profile — never against a real `~/.dsh`. From `0.2.2` the model-faci
ng tool list is assembled from the registry after the system-prompt waterfall, so the broker hides d
irect tools with `deferLoading`; `0.2.1-rc.5` still passes the list through the waterfall and is fil
tered there. The `0.2.*` entries additionally pass `node scripts/verify-deferral-dsh.mjs <prefix>` (
real web profile + mock MCP server, no model request); the `headless` boot was not repeated for them

.
- Windows 10/11: stdio commands are launched via `cmd.exe` so `.cmd` shims (`npx`, `uvx`) resolve
ws 10/11: stdio commands are launched via `cmd.exe` so `.cmd` shims (`npx`, `uvx`) resolve correctly
### What the agent sees
With on-demand mode off (the default), every connected server's tools appear as first-class tools, e
.g. for a server named `odin`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Tool results are projected back as native DSH content blocks; MCP `isError` results surface through
the registry's error path. Image blocks (`{ type: 'image', data, mimeType }`) are never forwarded ra
w — a raw MCP image block has no `attachment`, so it would crash the session on the next turn. Rende
ring is text-first: when the routed model declares image input, the host stores the image in DSH's d
urable attachment store and the block becomes a real `{ type: 'image', attachment }`; in every other
case (no attachment store, model without image input, non-canonical base64, or a media type outside
PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF) the image degrades to an `[image unavailable: …]` text placeholder. Text blocks
are preserved in order, and the same sanitizing applies to results returned through `mcp_execute_too
preserved in order, and the same sanitizing applies to results returned through `mcp_execute_tool`.
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations

- `resources` and `prompts` MCP capabilities are not bridged (tools only).
- On-demand filtering tar
gets `native` presentation. Code/PTC/both agents keep the full session-visible MCP catalog; their pr
esentation is read from the executor's prompt sections (and, on harnesses that still supply one, fro
m the waterfall payload). Exported SDK renderers provide no presentation-only catalog contract; see

the interface evidence and fallbacks. Full SDK compression remains open in #18.
- On DSH ≤ 0.2.2-rc.
1, on-demand filtering only collapses the schemas on routes whose model catalog declares `toolUpdate
` (deepseek-official). Providers without `toolUpdate` (an `llm-pi-ai` backend with `api: openai-comp
letions` is the common case) take the core's "immediately available tools" branch, which strips the
`deferLoading` marker after the plugin returns, so the full `mcp__*` schemas would reach the provide
r every request. Since v0.17.0 the plugin mitigates this itself: on such a route each native agent g
ets **per-agent shadow stubs** — same `mcp__<server>__<tool>` names with a short pointer description
and an empty arguments schema registered in the agent's own tool scope — so the request payload col
lapses to the broker's three tools plus the stubs instead of the full schemas (the #33 report measur
ed 82k tokens for 197 tools), while `mcp_search_tools`/`mcp_describe_tool` keep serving the full sch
emas from the plugin-owned registration store. Honoring routes (deepseek-official), code/PTC/both ag
ents, and any model-route resolution failure keep the previous full-surface behavior; the upstream c

ore fix (preserve or honor the `deferLoading` marker per adapter) remains the ri [长行截断]
- OAuth toke
ns live in a plain JSON file under `~/.dsh` — treat the file as a secret. Static bearer tokens and `
headerEnv` values are read from environment variables and never persisted. Workspace OAuth tokens li

ve in the same state file, never in the workspace's `mcp.json`.
[该节后续省略]
